free_text: The patient is a 73-year-old male with a high PSA of 14.5 ng/mL and a Gleason grade of 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). MRI shows a PI-RADS 5 lesion with no evidence of extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. He has pre-existing chronic kidney disease. Management requires clinical review to balance treatment benefit against patient preferences.
